title: Tortellini with Butternut, Broccoli & Red Lentils
source: Built for Jarred's kids - no cheese

2 servings: 1/4 cup dried RED lentils, rinsed (not green or brown - see notes)
1/4 small onion, chopped, or 1 clove garlic
1 tsp white (shiro) miso - or just 1/2 tsp salt
Salt, and a small squeeze of lemon at the end
4 servings: 1/2 cup dried RED lentils, rinsed (not green or brown - see notes)
1/2 small onion, chopped, or 2 cloves garlic
2 tsp white (shiro) miso - or just 1 tsp salt
Salt, and a squeeze of lemon at the end

steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Toss the squash with the olive oil and a good pinch of salt and spread it in a single layer on a sheet pan - crowded squash steams instead of browning. Roast 25-30 min, until the edges are genuinely caramelized. Add the chopped onion to the pan for the last 15 min.
Meanwhile, put the red lentils and the stock in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 min, until the lentils have collapsed completely and the whole thing looks like a loose puree.

Add the broccoli to the lentil pan for the LAST 4-5 minutes only, just until a knife goes through. Longer and it goes army green and starts tasting like broccoli - which is the thing you are trying to avoid.
Boil the tortellini from frozen while the squash finishes. RESERVE 1 CUP of the pasta water before draining.

Blend the roasted squash and onion with the lentils, broccoli and all their liquid, plus the butter, miso and nutmeg, until completely smooth - 45 seconds, longer than feels necessary. Any texture left is what a kid will find.
Taste and salt properly, then add a small squeeze of lemon - it lifts the whole thing out of flat-and-sweet.
Toss with the drained tortellini over low heat for a minute, thinning with the reserved pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats rather than clumps.
notes: NO CHEESE, ON PURPOSE - and it does not need it. Cheese in a sauce like this is doing four jobs: salt, fat, umami and body. Here the lentils give the body, the butter gives the fat, the miso gives the umami, and you salt it properly at the end. That is the whole swap. IF YOU WANT MORE OF THAT SAVOURY EDGE without dairy: 1-2 Tbsp nutritional yeast tastes genuinely cheesy; 1 Tbsp tahini or cashew butter adds the richness Parmesan was carrying; a teaspoon of soy sauce works in place of the miso. RED LENTILS ONLY. Red (or yellow) lentils have no skins, so they fall apart completely in 15 min and vanish into the sauce. Green, brown or French lentils hold their shape no matter how long you cook them - a kid will spot them and the texture is grainy. This matters more than any other choice in the recipe. ROAST THE SQUASH, DO NOT BOIL IT. Boiled squash tastes like baby food - watery and flat. The caramelized edges are where all the sweetness comes from, and the sweetness is the whole reason kids eat this. In a hurry, microwave it covered with 2 Tbsp water for 8 min and stir in 1 tsp of honey to make up for what you lost. BROCCOLI GOES IN LAST. Four to five minutes, no more. Overcooked broccoli turns the sauce a muddy olive colour and brings a sulphur smell that is exactly what gets a plate pushed away. WHAT ELSE CAN GO IN: roasted carrot or sweet potato (more sweetness, same colour); cauliflower (disappears completely); a peeled roasted red pepper (deeper, slightly smoky); white beans or a spoon of red lentils more for extra protein; a pinch of smoked paprika for the adults' bowls. Spinach or peas work but turn the sauce green instead of orange - fine if your kids do not care about colour, a dealbreaker if they do. PASTA WATER, NOT MORE STOCK, for thinning. The starch is what makes it cling to the tortellini instead of sliding off into a puddle. FOR THE ADULTS: brown a tablespoon of butter with a few sage leaves and spoon it over the top, plus black pepper and chilli flakes. FREEZES WELL - the sauce on its own, not with the pasta in it. Roast a whole bag of squash, make a double batch of sauce and freeze half in a jar; it is a 10-minute dinner later. Thin with water when reheating, it sets up thick in the fridge.
